NSF GRFP Awardees — Analysis Report

Generated 2026-07-28 18:11 from grfp_listings.csv

About this report

The underlying data is scraped from research.gov's public NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP) awardee list by grfp_scraper.py, covering every listed Offered Award and Honorable Mention from 1952 to 2026 (132316 records total). Each record has the awardee's name, baccalaureate institution, field of study, and (for later years only) their institutional affiliation at the time of application.

Questions this report is trying to answer:

  • Which undergraduate institutions produce the most GRFP awardees, and how has that changed over time?
  • How does the Offered Award / Honorable Mention split break down, and has that ratio shifted over the decades?
  • Which fields of study are most represented, and how do subfields break down within the top fields?
  • Where do awardees end up for grad school relative to where they did undergrad (for the subset with both fields populated)?
  • Do any awardees reapply and appear more than once across years?

Key findings

  • 132,316 GRFP records from 1952-2026, across 3,556 baccalaureate institutions (78,807 Offered Award / 53,509 Honorable Mention, 60%/40%).
  • The largest single baccalaureate feeder is Massachusetts Institute of Technology, with 2,095 awards.
  • Life Sciences is the most common broad discipline, at 25% of records.
  • The top-10-institution share of all awards moved from 29% in the 1950s to a low of 15% in the 2000s, and stands at 17% in the 2020s -- see Feeder-pool concentration.
  • 12.9% of awardees whose first record was an Honorable Mention later won an Offered Award (reuses name-matching flagged elsewhere as having common-name false-positive risk -- treat as a rough upper bound, not a precise rate).
  • Cross-referencing against NSF Postdoc Award data: 32 candidate match(es) across 26 distinct PrincipalInvestigator name(s) that match a GRFP awardee (14 scored 'plausible') -- see the postdoc cross-reference section for caveats on name-only matching.

Repeat appearances

Checked for the same normalized name (first + last token, case-insensitive) appearing on more than one row -- e.g. an Honorable Mention one year followed by an Offered Award another, which is common on reapplication. Matches are name-based only, not verified identity links, so common names may produce false positives.

14,959 normalized names appear on more than one row; the most repeated, Smith, David H, appears 17 times (1956, 1960, 1962, 1967, 1970, 1974, 1980, 1982, 1996, 1997, 2002, 2003, 2009, 2015). Separately, 12.9% of awardees whose first record was an Honorable Mention (5,829 of 45,198) later won an Offered Award.

GRFP alumni who became PIs

32 candidate match(es) across 26 distinct PI name(s), 14 scored 'plausible'. See below for per-match detail and caveats on name-only matching.

Checks whether the PrincipalInvestigator on an NSF Postdoctoral Award record matches a GRFP awardee's name. Name-only matching over a 75-year GRFP history is prone to false positives for common names -- treat "plausible" as a lead to verify independently (ORCID/bio page), not a confirmed identity match. "Individual fellow" rows are the postdoc recipient themselves; "Institutional PI" rows are a grant's lead investigator, who is not necessarily anyone's direct advisor -- this does not attempt to infer who anyone has mentored.
